problem: Building QA systems that can learn to reason over knowledge graphs from question-answer pairs alone is challenging due to noisy question expressions and the need for multi-hop logic reasoning.
method: Propose a unified deep learning architecture and an end-to-end variational learning algorithm that handles noise in questions and learns multi-hop reasoning simultaneously.
key_assumptions: A variational learning algorithm can effectively handle noise in questions while learning multi-hop reasoning.
The proposed architecture can capture both structured KG information and noisy question semantics.
main_contribution: A novel variational reasoning framework for KG-based QA that achieves state-of-the-art performance on a recent benchmark dataset and introduces new benchmark datasets for noisy and multi-hop reasoning.
datasets: New benchmark datasets for multi-hop reasoning, paraphrased questions, and human voice questions
metrics: Not specified in abstract; likely accuracy or hit@1
results: ["Achieves state-of-the-art performance on a recent benchmark dataset; yields promising results on new benchmark datasets."]

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: This work focuses on a variational deep learning architecture to handle question noise and learn multi-hop reasoning. Our idea enriches training triples with local context subgraphs from the same passage and adds an adaptive repair loop for one-hop failures, targeting training data enrichment and iterative correction rather than a variational learning algorithm.
